messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated error-rate detected in prod on /v1/generate. 5xx rate from baseline ~0.6% -> 11.7% over last 5m. p95 latency jumped from ~210ms to ~1.9s, p99 ~3.2s. Canary cohort (canary=true) shows highest tail. Paging #oncall :rotating_light:

jess: saw this too. investigating. recent canary deploy at 12:43 UTC (commit d7f3b2). canary traffic is ~15% of overall. pushing page to oncall. tagging ryan.

ryan: oncall here, taking it. first pass: 504/gateway-timeout and internal 5xx (502/503) burst. pulling traces for a few traces:
```
TraceID: 0x7f3b...
span: upstream.call -> latency 3.1s
error: upstream-read-timeout
```

ryan: quick curl against a healthy front: `curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> 504. repro locally from our edge.

jess: datadog snapshots show a cluster of hosts with high blocked threads and long event-loop latencies. K/V cache eviction alarms firing around same time. suspecting kv-affinity / cache hot-shard causing backend stalls. logs show many `kvcache.Lookup timeout` errors. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:45:03Z] svc-generate-12 ERROR kvcache: Lookup timeout (3000ms) key="prompt:abc123"
[2026-03-15T12:45:04Z] svc-generate-12 WARN request: stalled waiting for kv cache
[2026-03-15T12:45:05Z] svc-generate-15 ERROR upstream: read timeout
```

priya: if kv cache is blocking hot path, we can flip routing to skip kvcache for the canary traffic (fast but slightly more cost). two options: 1) flip canary routing to bypass kv cache, or 2) roll back the canary. which do we want for immediate mitigation?

ryan: prefer minimal blast radius. trying the routing flip first. command to update route policy (console API):
```
POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routes/route-prod-canary/actions
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN
Body: {"action":"set_kv_bypass","value":true}
```

ryan: attempted flip via console UI, got error 409 on rollout config (policy conflicts with autoscaler). not safe to change live rollout quickly.

priya: given that, recommend rollback the canary to restore SLOs quickly. rollback will revert to previous stable commit c6a9e1. scope: canary only -> full rollback of canary cohort. impact: brief 30-60s rolling restarts for canary instances, no DB schema changes.

ryan: executing rollback now. tagging @deploy-bot to perform the rollout rollback.

deploy-bot: Received rollback request: target=canary, from=d7f3b2 -> to=c6a9e1. Initiating. Rolling hosts (3 hosts in canary pool) sequentially (drain -> replace). ETA ~ 4m. :gear:

deploy-bot: Host svc-generate-canary-01 rolled back (drain ok).

deploy-bot: Host svc-generate-canary-02 rolled back (drain ok).

deploy-bot: Host svc-generate-canary-03 rolled back (drain ok). Rollback complete.

infra-sre: monitoring graphs now. p95 down from 1.9s -> 260ms within ~2m of rollback. 5xx rate down to 0.9% and falling. p99 ~380ms.

emma-support: opened 5 inbound tickets flagged as incidents from enterprise customers (account ids x-112, x-117). informed them we detected a regression, rolled the canary back, and are continuing RMS. Customers asked for root cause and ETA for RCA. they appreciate the quick mitigation.

jess: good. creating incident ticket INC-21246 with timeline and actions, assigning to infra-sre for RCA (kv-affinity hypothesis) and to infra/serving for follow-up on safe rollout gating.

ryan: follow-ups: 1) run thorough kvcache health and eviction analysis, look for hot key patterns; 2) add a gating check that prevents canary rollouts if kv cache eviction rate > threshold; 3) add an ops runbook step to switch routing to bypass kvcache in emergencies (and ensure rollout config allows it).

jess: agreed. also notify PS and account teams for affected customers, and schedule postmortem. closing this Slack thread when INC-21246 is created. :white_check_mark:
